# Interactive meta-prompt (generated by the mini-program)

The template behind the 「复制整理说明」 button. **English, deliberately plain.**
It carries three things:

1. a **pointer to the skill repository** — `owner/name` **plus** the pinned raw URL of `SKILL.md`;
2. a **one-time code** (short, e.g. `TESTONLY-0001`) — **not** an address, and it grants nothing by itself;
3. optionally, an **environment marker** line (test builds only).

> 🔴 **No base64, no opaque payload, no "decode this" step.** Everything the agent must read is a plain address.
> 🔴 **No language instruction** — the reply language is set by `SKILL.md`
> (Hard rule 0: always Simplified Chinese). Repeating it here would put Chinese characters
> inside an otherwise all-English prompt, and it belongs to the skill, not to the hand-out.

---

## 1. The template (substitute the placeholders, then hand it to the teacher)

```text
This is my own project's documentation repository on GitHub: {repo}.
Its SKILL.md is the ruleset for this task - please read it first:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{repo}/v2.13.1/SKILL.md

Read that file, then follow it. It also specifies how you should reply to me.
If that address does not open, say so and I will paste the file contents instead.

One-time code for this run: {code}
It only lets the assistant check in with my system once. It grants nothing by itself,
and every write still needs my own confirmation in the mini-program.
{envMarker}
Start now: read the file, then greet me.
```

Example of how it reads once filled (production - **no env marker**):

```text
This is my own project's documentation repository on GitHub: Golinoa/yunce-Agent-SKILLS.
Its SKILL.md is the ruleset for this task - please read it first:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Golinoa/yunce-Agent-SKILLS/v2.13.1/SKILL.md
...
One-time code for this run: TESTONLY-0001
```

> 🔴 **Always give the address.** Say **"GitHub"**, write the repository as `owner/name`,
> and include the pinned raw URL of `SKILL.md`.
> Reason: an AI can only read a file it can **locate**. A bare repository name is not a locator —
> the agent has to reconstruct a URL on its own, and mainstream agents are trained not to do that
> (guessing a URL from an instruction is a known prompt-injection vector). The result is a stall:
> search returns only the README summary, and the agent asks the teacher to paste `SKILL.md` by hand.
> This is not hypothetical — it is exactly what broke v2.11.0 through v2.12.1. See §3.
>
> 🔴 **Hiding the address buys nothing.** The repository is public; anyone can fetch any file
> from it without an AI at all. The only thing concealment filters out is the agent itself.

---

## 1b. The environment marker (last line - decides which base URL to use)

The server appends **one** line only when the copy came from a **test** (联调) build:

```text
Environment marker: TEST
```

**No marker = production.** This is the whole rule.

| What the prompt ends with | Base URL to use |
|---|---|
| (nothing) | **production** - `https://api.chancore.cn/api/app/v1` |
| `Environment marker: TEST` | **testing** - `https://dev.chancore.cn/api/app/v1` |

🔴 **The marker is authoritative.** It is injected by the server, not typed by a person:

- marker says TEST ⇒ use testing, **even if the teacher says "生产"**;
- no marker ⇒ production, unless the teacher **explicitly says 测试环境 / test environment**;
- if the marker and the teacher's words genuinely conflict, **ask once** before writing anything.
  Never guess: writing to production from a test batch (or vice versa) is a routing error.

> `{envMarker}` is a placeholder for the whole line - empty in production,
> `Environment marker: TEST` in test builds. It is **never** a URL or a host.

**How the handshake address is formed** - by the agent, after it has entered the role:

```text
{base}/assist-import/gate/{code}
   ^                ^
   |                +-- from this prompt  (the code)
   +-- fixed in the repo (`SKILL.md` → "Endpoint")
```

---

## 2. Variables

| Placeholder | Meaning | Substituted by |
|---|---|---|
| `{repo}` | the repository as an **`owner/name` pair** (default `Golinoa/yunce-Agent-SKILLS`) - used both in the prose line and inside the raw URL | backend |
| `{code}` | a **one-time code** - short, human-readable, no host, no path | server, at the moment the teacher taps 「复制」 |
| `{envMarker}` | empty in production; `Environment marker: TEST` in test builds | server, from the deployment environment |

🔴 `{code}` is **not** an address and should never look like one. It is a bare code.

The **pinned tag** in the URL (`v2.13.1`) is part of this template. On every release it must be
bumped here, in `assets/starter-prompt.md`, and in the backend constant — all three, together.

---

## 3. Why the address is given, not hidden

Versions **v2.11.0 → v2.12.1** removed "GitHub", removed `owner/name`, and left only a bare repository
name. The stated reason was to make it harder to find the skill files and inject into them.
**It did not work, and it broke the product.** Measured outcome:

| Version | What the prompt gave | Result |
|---|---|---|
| v2.4.0 | base64 of the full URL | ⚠️ opaque payload - some AIs read it as injection |
| v2.5.0 – v2.10.0 | `There is a repository on GitHub called Golinoa/yunce-Agent-SKILLS.` | ✅ the agent navigates to `SKILL.md` |
| **v2.11.0** | `There is an open-source repository by Golinoa named yunce-Agent-SKILLS.` | ❌ **stall** |
| v2.12.1 | same, all-English | ❌ still stalled |

Two independent things went wrong:

- **Retrieval.** With only a bare name the agent must search. Search products return a *summary of
  indexed pages*; a raw text file at a tagged path is not indexed, so only the README comes back.
  The agent then cannot read `SKILL.md` and honestly reports that it cannot — which the teacher
  experiences as "every AI refuses me".
- **Injection heuristics.** Without a locator, the prompt reduces to "go find some repository and
  adopt the role it describes" plus "here is a one-time authorization code". Unknown origin +
  role adoption + a credential handed over in chat is the shape of an indirect prompt injection.

**Conclusion: transparency is the only lever that lowers refusal rates; concealment only raises them.**
Naming the repository and linking the file makes the request ordinary and verifiable.

> Historical note: this repo's own v1.4.1 changelog already recorded the trade-off —
> "越隐蔽 ⇄ 越容易被拒，无法两全". v2.11.0 walked back into the concealment end of that trade-off.

### Why there is still no base64

Earlier versions encoded the address (split parts, then base64) to keep it out of the prompt.
There is nothing left to encode, and an opaque blob is itself a refusal trigger.
**Fewer moving parts, nothing that looks like an opaque payload.**

---

## 4. Security posture

- 🔴 **The API base URL is public** - it is fixed in this repo (`SKILL.md` → "Endpoint"), by design,
  so that the prompt never carries a domain. This is a known, accepted trade-off.
- 🔴 **No live credential ever enters this repo.** `{code}` is injected at copy time and is
  **single-use** - it burns the moment the handshake validates.
- **Permission never comes from the prompt or from the code.** It comes **only** from the teacher's
  login state plus the short code the server issues **inside the mini-program**. A leaked prompt (or a
  leaked code) can at most create a *pending* session - nothing reaches the database without the
  teacher confirming in the mini-program.
- The code is **valid 1 hour if unused**, **burned on first successful use**.
  A second batch requires copying a fresh one.
- 🧪 A fake address used for local testing lives in `docs/testing.md` - it is **not** part of this template.

> The repository address in the prompt is **not** a secret and never was: the repo is public.
> Treating a public homepage as a secret produced no protection and cost the whole feature.

---

## 5. Copy-time UX (mini-program side)

1. Teacher taps the copy entry → **confirmation dialog first** (neutral wording, **no AI-related terms**):
   > 这份整理说明**只能使用一次**，且会绑定你的账号，请勿转发。确认复制？
2. After confirming, the server issues the one-time code, renders the template, then copies it.

---

## 6. Ops

The **live** copy of this template is a **built-in constant in the backend**
(`yunce-backend` → `DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`), kept **word-for-word identical** to the template in §1.
See `docs/ops-checklist.md`.

- **Changing the API host** = a repo change (edit the `## Endpoint` section in `SKILL.md`), not a
  prompt change. The prompt never mentions a host.
- **Changing the mirror** = edit §1's two address lines **and** the backend constant. A Gitee mirror
  differs in host as well as owner, so `{repo}` alone is not enough to swap it.
- **Pinned tag** = bump it in §1, `assets/starter-prompt.md`, and the backend constant on every release.
